newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco says making progress in Sudbury talks.
newsitem.headline: Inco says making progress in Sudbury talks.

text.p: Canadian nickel giant Inco Ltd said on Monday it is making progress in contract talks with the union representing workers in its Ontario operations.
"We feel there is progress toward an agreement," Inco spokesman Jerry Rodgers told Reuters in a telephone interview from Sudbury.
The United Steelworkers of America said earlier on Monday that it had requested the assistance of a provincial mediator after talks reached an impasse on Saturday.
The current contract between Inco and 4700 workers expires at midnight May 31.
Rodgers declined to comment further on the state of negotiations with the union.
"We worked on the weekend and we're meeting again today. We feel we are making progress," he said.
The last time the union requested mediation was in 1982.
Fraser said contract talks reached an impasse on Saturday.
Workers at Inco's Ontario operations have voted 98 percent in favor of giving union leaders a mandate to strike if a tentative agreement cannot be reached by May 31.
The contract affects 4,700 workers at the nickel giant's mining, smelting and refinery operations in Sudbury and its refinery in Port Colborne.
